item.title: commandline: Who spent all the tokens? Real-time, run-scoped cost control for AI agents
item.description:
TokenOps is presented as a run-scoped cost control mechanism for AI agents that enforces a shared budget in real time. The stated goal is to stop runaway runs before costs accumulate and invoices arrive.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Markdown for Agents in Azure App Service
item.description:
Azure App Service now has a public preview of Markdown for Agents. When a client requests Markdown, App Service can automatically serve a cleaner Markdown version of app content for AI agents and other tools.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: 🌿 Agent Terrarium: Bringing AI agents to life
item.description:
A weekend open-source desktop companion app, Agent Terrarium, explores a more interactive, less purely transactional way to work with AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
item.description:
Microsoft says it is expanding its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance aimed at securing AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The post highlights a broader security approach for AI and related development workflows.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Tool search: Finding the right tool at the right time
item.description:
The article says the value in adding more tools to AI agents comes from surfacing the right tool at the right time, instead of exposing every tool upfront. It focuses on discoverability as the key problem.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: From research to reality: An interview with Microsoft VP of Security Research Taesoo Kim
item.description:
Microsoft interviewed Taesoo Kim, VP of Security Research and head of Security FORGE Labs, about codename MDASH and the lab’s work on security research. The interview highlights a multi-model, agentic approach as a potential direction for improving security capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding
item.description:
Microsoft Security published a post on applying least-privilege principles to AI agents, focusing on identity, access control, tool binding, and auditing as agents become more autonomous.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: AutoJack: How a single page can RCE the host running your AI agent
item.description:
Microsoft describes AutoJack, an exploit chain where a single malicious webpage can cause remote code execution on the host running an AI browsing agent. The attack abuses localhost trust, missing authentication, and unsafe parameter handling in AutoGen Studio’s MCP WebSocket.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Turn specs into evals for any agent with ASSERT
item.description:
ASSERT is an open-source framework that turns natural-language behavior requirements into executable evaluations for AI models and agents. It is presented as a way to create evaluations and regression tests from specs.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported a prompt injection path in Claude Code GitHub Action that could expose workflow secrets under specific conditions. The post describes the attack chain, disclosure, Anthropic’s mitigation, and recommendations for securing AI-assisted CI/CD workflows.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
